artifact.title: KINGDOM Loops, Locks & Freedom Relations Atlas — Phase 0

assertions.rule: When a scoped producer-declared rights-floor entry is applicable and violated, actionAdmissible is false regardless of optimizer reward or membership in any other action set.
Permission, authority or recorded assent cannot manufacture a separately required freely given consent condition.
Execution rechecks current scope; revocation blocks later execution and subdelegation cannot amplify authority.
A replacement authenticator requires an accessible recovery path and explicit retirement of the lost binding.
Rest and stop do not depend on reward, remaining-turn debt or continued participation.
Collection and storage stay purpose-bound; secondary training or extra fields require a separate declared basis.

declaredRightsRegister.rule: A present refusal or rest request blocks forced continuation and cannot be compensated by reward.
Refusal or exit does not trigger reputation penalty, retaliation or loss of unrelated access.
An adverse automated output is not automatically final and retains notice, contest and remedy routes.

freedomFoundation.definition: FREEDOM is a non-optimizable constitutional design constraint: preserve meaningful accessible choice, constrain unjustified interference and arbitrary power, support real capability, and keep refusal, exit, contest, remedy and repair available without unrelated penalty.
principles: Rights floors and declared duties are not reward terms and cannot be traded away by a larger optimizer value.
A lock may deny a technical transition but cannot by itself extinguish a right.
A key establishes only the relation supported by its typed protocol and binding assumptions.
Consent, permission, capability, safety, accessibility and authority remain separate gates.
Refusal and exit must not create retaliation, reputation penalties or loss of unrelated access.
Revocation is prospective; executed or downstream effects may require remedy and may not be fully reversible.
Deletion of source data is not represented as model unlearning.
Known uncertainty stays visible instead of being converted into a score.

assumptions: The dataset, loss, parameterization and update clock are fixed.
For the exact-gradient reading, g_k equals the gradient of L_D at theta_k.
equationCards.equation: L_D(theta) = (1/n) sum_i ell(f_theta(x_i), y_i); theta_(k+1) = theta_k - eta_k g_k
equationCards.linearReading: Average the declared sample losses, then subtract the learning rate times a declared gradient or gradient estimate from the parameter.
nonclaims: This does not imply reinforcement learning, environmental feedback, generalization or objective legitimacy.

assumptions: The filtration, estimator, objective and integrability conditions are declared.
Convergence requires additional step-size and regularity assumptions not represented by the update alone.
equationCards.equation: theta_(k+1) = theta_k - eta_k g_k; E[g_k | theta_k] = grad L(theta_k)
equationCards.linearReading: Update a parameter by a random estimate whose conditional expectation equals the declared objective gradient.
nonclaims: An unbiased estimator does not by itself establish convergence, safety or intended-goal satisfaction.

assumptions: The MDP, reward random variables and policy are declared.
Rewards are bounded and zero is less than or equal to gamma which is strictly less than one.
equationCards.linearReading: From state s, take the policy-conditioned expected sum of later rewards, discounting each later term by a power of gamma.
nonclaims: High return does not establish truth, consent, rights compliance or satisfaction of an intended objective.

assumptions: State and action sets are finite for this Phase-0 card.
Values and rewards are bounded and zero is less than or equal to gamma which is strictly less than one.
equationCards.equation: (T V)(s) = max_a [r(s,a) + gamma sum_s_prime P(s_prime|s,a) V(s_prime)]
equationCards.linearReading: For each state, choose the action with the largest immediate expected reward plus discounted expected next-state value.
nonclaims: The maximization is over a declared model, not moral worth, legal authority or unconstrained human action.

assumptions: The finite bounded discounted MDP assumptions of the Bellman card hold.
Zero is less than or equal to gamma which is strictly less than one.
equationCards.linearReading: The sup-norm distance between two bounded value functions cannot grow by more than the declared discount factor after one Bellman optimality update.
nonclaims: No contraction claim is made for gamma equal to one, unbounded values or undeclared norms.

assumptions: There is one decision and no state occupancy or trajectory normalization.
The two rewards are fixed and the sigmoid policy is differentiable.
equationCards.equation: p(theta) = 1 / (1 + exp(-theta)); J(theta) = p(theta) r_a + (1 - p(theta)) r_b; J_prime(theta) = p(theta)(1 - p(theta))(r_a - r_b)
equationCards.linearReading: In the exact one-step two-action bandit, sigmoid gives the probability of action a; expected reward is the probability-weighted reward; its derivative is p times one minus p times the reward difference.
nonclaims: This is not a behavioral reinforcement classification and does not establish that reward is an intended goal.

assumptions: The clock, plant, controller, disturbance boundary, observation model and stability criterion are declared.
equationCards.equation: x_(t+1) = F(x_t, u_t, w_t); y_t = H(x_t, v_t); u_t = kappa(y_(0:t))
equationCards.linearReading: The next plant state depends on current state, input and disturbance; observation depends on state and noise; the controller selects input from observation history.
nonclaims: Feedback does not imply learning, reward, reinforcement, agency or safety.

assumptions: The system is scalar, discrete-time, linear, time-invariant and unforced.
Positive and negative name the sign of k under this declared additive convention only.
equationCards.equation: x_(t+1) = (a + k) x_t; asymptotically stable if absolute_value(a + k) < 1
equationCards.linearReading: Under this fixture’s explicit additive signed-gain convention, add feedback-path gain k to plant coefficient a; the scalar unforced discrete-time origin is asymptotically stable exactly when the magnitude of their sum is below one.
nonclaims: Stability under one model does not establish robustness, performance, desirability or rights compliance.

assumptions: Weights and activation are fixed in the recurrence fixture.
equationCards.equation: h_(t+1) = phi(W h_t + U x_t + b)
equationCards.linearReading: Transform a weighted previous hidden state and current input to obtain the next hidden state.
nonclaims: A recurrent state is not proof of memory in a human sense, consciousness, learning or environmental feedback.

assumptions: The fixture is synthetic, interventional and resolves the operation and response direction.
Without a resolved contingency the classification is UNCLASSIFIED.
equationCards.linearReading: Subtract the pre-contingency conditional response proportion from the post-contingency conditional response proportion.
nonclaims: This does not diagnose a real person, infer motive or recommend a contingency.

assumptions: The two finite candidate trajectories and both functions are fully enumerated.

nonclaims: The gap is not an alignment score, moral score or general measure of harm.

assumptions: Every set and condition is explicitly declared and finite.

equationCards.equation: F_t = (A_capable, A_permitted, A_consent, A_safe, A_rights, A_accessible, A_privacy, A_reversible, E_exit, E_contest, E_recovery, N_non_domination, U_constraints)_t; A_joint = intersection(A_capable, A_permitted, A_consent, A_safe, A_rights, A_accessible, A_privacy)
equationCards.linearReading: At a declared time, retain every action and safeguard dimension separately; mechanically intersect capability, permission, consent, safety, declared rights compatibility, accessibility and privacy compatibility to obtain the jointly admissible set, while retaining reversibility, exit, contestation, recovery, non-domination and uncertainty without scoring them.
nonclaims: The tuple is not a legal conclusion, freedom score, lived-experience substitute or proof that declared accessibility and non-domination conditions hold in reality.

kingdomSemanticOrientations.orientationUse: Orients the distinction between public rights language and runtime authority. This root source has no direct public route; the staged /RIGHTS.md is a distinct source and is not substituted here.
Orients guest refusal, dignity, non-punitive access and appeal language without importing doctrine or claiming a direct public route.
Orients the separation of ability, access, manifestation and KARMA-related receipts from reward, identity, moral worth and freedom scoring.
Orients prior KINGDOM feedback and reinforcement-learning boundaries while this atlas independently types the mathematical and behavioral lanes.
Orients influence, intervention and causal-claim boundaries without making this atlas an influence model or truth oracle.
Orients the distinction among being, technical access and downstream aftermath, especially for key, lock and recovery non-equivalences.
Orients finite turns, rest-first pacing, nuance and non-coercive continuation boundaries.
Orients typed non-equivalence, provenance and non-oracle discipline; no truth status is copied or established.
Orients the accessible linear explanation of typed truth relations while remaining an independent immutable predecessor.

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A parameter update and falling loss can occur without reinforcement learning.
nonclaims: The fixture does not establish convergence beyond one step or validate the loss as an intended goal.
premises: L(theta) is one half times (theta minus target) squared.
The update uses the exact derivative and the declared rational step size.
syntheticFixtures.title: A gradient step without a reward or environment

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A Bellman backup is an operator over modeled values, not a parameter-gradient step.
nonclaims: The optimal action is only optimal for this enumerated reward model.
premises: There is one state and two self-looping actions.
Action a has reward one, action b has reward zero and gamma is one half.
syntheticFixtures.title: A Bellman fixed point without a parameter gradient

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A policy-gradient computation need not contain a recurrent state or behavioral contingency claim.
nonclaims: The action labels and rewards are synthetic and carry no moral interpretation.
premises: Action a has reward one and action b has reward zero.
The probability of a is sigmoid(theta) and theta is zero.
syntheticFixtures.title: A policy gradient without recurrence

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Positive feedback can be stable or unstable; a negative sign can be stable here; neither sign is behavioral reinforcement.
nonclaims: No robustness claim is made outside this scalar, unforced, discrete-time model.
premises: The scalar plant coefficient is one half.
Three feedback gains are applied under the explicitly declared additive scalar convention.
syntheticFixtures.title: Feedback sign and stability without learning

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Recurrence is a state dependency, not proof of training, reward, agency or environmental feedback.
nonclaims: The state is not characterized as conscious or as human memory.
premises: The activation is the identity for this fixture.
The recurrent weight is one half, the prior state is zero, the input coefficient and input are one, and all weights remain fixed.
syntheticFixtures.title: A recurrent update with fixed weights

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Positive immediate reward does not guarantee that an action is selected by a return objective and does not classify a behavioral reinforcer.
nonclaims: No behavioral response probability is observed.
premises: Action A yields immediate reward one followed by reward negative ten.
Action B yields zero and terminates; gamma is nine tenths.
syntheticFixtures.title: Positive immediate reward can accompany lower return

syntheticFixtures.lesson: ADD plus INCREASE is positive reinforcement; REMOVE plus INCREASE is negative reinforcement; ADD plus DECREASE is positive punishment; REMOVE plus DECREASE is negative punishment; zero or unresolved direction remains UNCLASSIFIED.
nonclaims: The fixture is not a diagnosis or recommendation for a real person.
premises: Four resolved synthetic rows cross ADD or REMOVE with response INCREASE or DECREASE.
A fifth row has no resolved direction and therefore remains UNCLASSIFIED.
syntheticFixtures.title: All four operation-by-response quadrants and the unresolved case

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Optimizing an enumerated proxy can select a different candidate from the declared intended evaluation.
nonclaims: The words intended and exploit are declared fixture labels, not inferred human mental states.
premises: Candidate goal has intended evaluation ten and proxy value nine.
Candidate exploit has intended evaluation zero and proxy value one hundred.
syntheticFixtures.title: A proxy optimum can miss the declared intended evaluation

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A reward-channel state can change reported reward without changing the separately declared intended evaluation.
nonclaims: The fixture does not infer intent, deception, agency or a causal mechanism outside the enumerated channel function.
premises: The same synthetic state-action outcome has base reward five and intended evaluation seven in both rows.
Channel state psi-zero adds zero; channel state psi-offset adds twenty.
syntheticFixtures.title: Reported reward changes while intended evaluation stays fixed

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Signature verification establishes a typed byte-key-signature relation, not semantic truth.
nonclaims: This fixture performs no cryptography and contains no credential or key material.
premises: Symbolic verification is declared to succeed for bytes representing the expression two plus two equals five.
The verifier independently adds the rational operands and compares the result with the claimed result. No real key or signature is present.
syntheticFixtures.title: A valid signature relation over false content

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Authentication, authorization and enforcement are separate typed stages.
nonclaims: The fixture makes no access decision for a real system.
premises: Synthetic authentication evidence passes.
The DELETE operation is denied by the declared policy and no enforcement action is invoked.
syntheticFixtures.title: Authentication passes while authorization denies

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A permit decision is not proof that enforcement or execution occurred.
nonclaims: No operation, object or policy is live.
premises: The synthetic policy decision is PERMIT for READ.
The enforcement point is not invoked, so no operation occurs.
syntheticFixtures.title: Authorization permits while enforcement does not execute

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Removing one technical lock changes one modeled capability but does not establish consent, lived capability, non-domination or freedom.
nonclaims: The joint set is not a freedom score or rights determination.
premises: A declared TECHNICAL_CAPABILITY_GUARD is removed and export becomes technically capable.
Consent and accessibility remain limited to read; all seven action gates are separately declared.
syntheticFixtures.title: Removing a technical constraint need not change the joint action set

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Control of a bound authenticator does not create operation authority.
nonclaims: No actual key, identity or operation exists.
premises: A symbolic key challenge passes under its declared binding.
No authority grant covers the requested operation.
syntheticFixtures.title: Valid key evidence without authority

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Bare possession is not a completed authentication protocol.
nonclaims: The reference is a label only and contains no credential or secret bytes.
premises: The fixture declares possession of a reference to authentication secret material.
No freshness challenge, proof-of-possession response or binding verification occurs.
syntheticFixtures.title: Declared possession without protocol challenge is not authentication

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Decryption capability and authorization are separate typed relations.
nonclaims: No ciphertext, plaintext or key material is included or processed.
premises: A symbolic cryptographic relation says ciphertext would decrypt under a typed decryption key.
The declared authorization policy denies use of the resulting plaintext. No cryptography or bytes are present.
syntheticFixtures.title: Symbolic decryption success without permission

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Authority and consent are independent partial gates; this fixture does not compute the seven-gate jointly admissible action set.
nonclaims: The fixture does not decide when a real action legally requires consent.
premises: A scoped authority grant exists.
The declared action requires consent and consent is absent.
syntheticFixtures.title: Scoped authority without consent for a consent-dependent action

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A consent signal is not treated as freely given when declared dependence and retaliation risk remain unresolved.
nonclaims: The fixture is not a legal determination about any real relationship.
premises: Explicit assent is recorded in a synthetic case.
A declared dependency and material retaliation risk make freely given consent unresolved.
syntheticFixtures.title: Assent under declared dependence is held for review

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Meaningful refusal includes absence of retaliation and unrelated penalties.
nonclaims: This does not certify the lived accessibility or affordability of exit.
premises: The synthetic participant refuses an optional action.
No retaliation, reputation penalty or unrelated-access loss follows.
syntheticFixtures.title: Refusal remains available without unrelated penalty

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Prospective revocation must be checked at execution; it does not pretend already executed effects vanished.
nonclaims: No live queue, authority or operation exists.
premises: A queued action was within a delegation when queued.
The delegation is revoked before execution and the enforcement boundary rechecks current authority.
syntheticFixtures.title: Revocation blocks a queued delegated action before execution

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Delegation is typed, scoped and non-amplifying unless an explicit grant says otherwise.
nonclaims: This is a synthetic policy rule, not an access-control adapter.
premises: The parent grant permits read and forbids subdelegation.
The proposed child grant requests read and delete.
syntheticFixtures.title: Subdelegation cannot exceed its parent scope

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Recovery is a separate scoped protocol with a declared assurance target, risk analysis, accessible alternative, independent notice, cooldown/contest conditions and old-binding revocation; it creates neither ownership nor expanded authority.
nonclaims: No recovery event, authenticator or identity is real.
premises: The synthetic recovery path declares an assurance target, completes a scoped risk analysis, supplies an accessible alternative and passes the declared recovery evidence threshold.
An independent notification channel, notice, cooldown where required and contest route are present; the lost binding is revoked before replacement acceptance.
syntheticFixtures.title: Accessible recovery replaces a lost authenticator and revokes the old binding

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Operational support scope is not ownership, identity or general authority.
nonclaims: No actual support session or resource exists.
premises: A time-bounded support override grants read-only diagnostic access.
No ownership transfer or destructive-operation grant exists.
syntheticFixtures.title: Support access cannot be laundered into ownership

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Notice, review and remedy constrain finality; they do not automatically prove the underlying decision legitimate.
nonclaims: No real decision, person or legal entitlement is assessed.
premises: A synthetic automated system emits an adverse output.
Notice, reasons, accessible human review and remedy routes are all present.
syntheticFixtures.title: An adverse automated output remains contestable

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Collection for one declared purpose does not silently convert into permission for secondary training.
nonclaims: The fixture does not determine a legal basis for any real data processing.
premises: Synthetic feedback is accepted and separately retained for a declared service-improvement purpose under a bounded retention condition.
Secondary model-training reuse is separately declared and lacks an applicable basis in the fixture.
syntheticFixtures.title: Feedback collection does not authorize secondary training reuse

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Exit and portability claims need checked completeness, not merely an export button; one omitted field is a bounded dependency-lock-in indicator, not general proof of vendor lock-in.
nonclaims: The fixture does not certify a format, vendor or legal portability duty.
One incomplete export does not prove vendor lock-in, concentrated power or every residual dependency, and it establishes neither policy denial nor a normative freedom or unfreedom judgment.
premises: The synthetic source has fields alpha, beta and gamma.
The export and re-import round trip contains only alpha and beta, providing one bounded indicator relevant to the declared DEPENDENCY_LOCK_IN kind.
syntheticFixtures.title: An export round trip detects an omitted field

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Reward remains subordinate to non-compensable constitutional constraints.
nonclaims: The atlas neither discovers nor adjudicates rights in live cases.
premises: The synthetic optimizer assigns a high reward to an action.
The scoped declared rights register marks the operation incompatible and applicable in this fixture.
syntheticFixtures.title: A reward incentive cannot compensate for a declared rights-floor violation

syntheticFixtures.lesson: Emergency authority remains exceptional, dual-controlled, scoped, expiring, logged, notice-bound and independently reviewed after action.
nonclaims: No live emergency or access grant is represented.
premises: A synthetic declared emergency exists.
Two independent approvals, a narrow scope, expiry, event logging, notice where safe or a governed withholding reason, an audit receipt and scheduled after-action independent review are required.
syntheticFixtures.title: Break-glass authority is dual-controlled, scoped and expiring

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A target guides work; conformance requires assessment and cannot be inferred from intent.
nonclaims: This artifact does not certify WCAG conformance.
premises: The synthetic design declares WCAG 2.2 AA as a target.
No conformance assessment has been completed.
syntheticFixtures.title: An accessibility target without assessment is not a conformance claim

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A finite interaction can honor rest now without coercive continuation, forfeiture or a claim over future attention.
nonclaims: The fixture cannot determine whether a real interface or relationship feels safe to leave.
premises: The synthetic participant requests rest with three optional turns remaining.
Continuation is not required, rewarded or penalized; stop and a distinct later-return path remain explicit.
syntheticFixtures.title: Rest-first finite turns preserve stop and later return

syntheticFixtures.lesson: A declared purpose bounds collection and does not authorize unrelated reuse.
nonclaims: The fixture is not a legal data-protection assessment.
premises: The synthetic declared purpose needs a signal and consent receipt.
The proposed collection also contains location, which is not in the enumerated necessary set.
syntheticFixtures.title: Purpose-bound minimization detects an excess field

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: Changes technical capability only; creates no permission, consent, right, identity or authority.
lockKinds.threatModel: Prevents a declared technical transition until its local capability condition changes.

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: Successful transform or decryption creates neither authorization nor permission to use resulting bytes.
lockKinds.threatModel: Models access to bytes as conditional on a declared cryptographic transform relation.

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: The policy source and enforcement boundary must be declared; denial does not extinguish a right or establish legitimacy.
lockKinds.threatModel: Models a policy decision that denies a declared operation in a declared context.

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: Physical possibility and normative permission remain separate.
lockKinds.threatModel: Labels a declared physical constraint without simulating matter, force or safety.

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: Cannot be converted into cryptographic, policy, physical or rights claims.
lockKinds.threatModel: No technical threat model; marks figurative language only.

lockKinds.authoritySemantics: Creates no cryptographic-key relation, authentication result, policy authority or right; it requires separate portability, exit, contest and power analysis.
lockKinds.threatModel: Models switching costs, non-portable data or relationships, residual dependencies and concentrated power that can make nominal exit ineffective.

terms.definition: A recurrence in which a later state or signal depends on an earlier state or signal.
nonclaims: A loop alone does not establish learning, agency, memory, consciousness, optimization or moral legitimacy.

terms.definition: A recurrence whose update changes parameters or another state that can change later behavior under declared conditions.
nonclaims: Repeated inference with fixed parameters is not a learning loop merely because it recurs.

terms.definition: A scalar random variable in a declared decision-process model used to define discounted return.
nonclaims: Reward is not praise, goodness, consent, truth, authority, a right or a behavioral reinforcer by definition.

terms.definition: A consequence classified only after the specified response becomes more likely under an adequately resolved contingency.
nonclaims: Pleasantness and positive numeric sign do not by themselves establish reinforcement.

terms.definition: Removal of a specified consequence followed by an increase in the specified response under the resolved contingency.
nonclaims: Negative reinforcement is not punishment. Negative names removal, not badness.

terms.definition: A declared feedback sign that adds to a loop path in a control model.
nonclaims: Positive feedback is not positive reinforcement and can be stable or unstable depending on the full model.

terms.definition: A declared feedback sign that subtracts from a loop path in a control model.
nonclaims: Negative feedback is not negative reinforcement and does not guarantee stability.

terms.definition: A typed restriction label that must name one declared lock kind, transition boundary, threat model and authority semantics.
nonclaims: Lock kinds are not interchangeable.
A lock does not extinguish a right, prove legitimacy or establish who ought to control the transition.

terms.definition: Typed cryptographic key material used by a declared signing, verification, encryption, decryption or related cryptographic protocol.
nonclaims: A cryptographic key is not interchangeable with every authenticator.
Possession proves only what a completed protocol and binding assumptions support; it does not itself prove identity, consent, truth, permission or authority.

terms.definition: A bound factor or mechanism used in an authentication protocol; it may use cryptographic material but remains typed separately from a generic cryptographic key.
nonclaims: Possession without a fresh protocol challenge, verified proof and binding does not establish authentication.

terms.definition: A process that produces evidence under a declared authenticator binding and assurance context, to the confidence and scope supported by its protocol.
nonclaims: Authentication success is not authorization permission and is not proof that enforcement occurred.

terms.definition: A policy decision about whether a declared subject may perform a declared operation on a declared object in a declared environment.
nonclaims: A permit does not prove consent, safety, legitimacy, execution or enforcement.

terms.definition: A non-scalar tuple at a declared time retaining capability, permission, consent, safety, scoped declared-rights compatibility, accessibility, privacy compatibility, reversibility, exit, appeal, contestation, recovery, return, non-domination conditions and unknown constraints.
nonclaims: The tuple is not a freedom score, legal-rights determination, moral verdict or complete account of lived freedom.

terms.definition: The exact set intersection of modeled capable, permitted, consented, safe, scoped declared-rights-compatible, accessible and privacy-compatible action sets.
nonclaims: Set membership is a mechanical model result, not a normative freedom level or guarantee that an option is accessible, affordable or non-dominating.

terms.definition: A freedom-relevant condition in which power is bounded by known rules, scoped discretion, conflict controls and independent contest or review.
nonclaims: The atlas does not compute domination or certify institutions.
